briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Repeal Momentum Builds in Lansing While Psychedelics Go Mainstream in D.C.
briefs.top: Michigan operators are getting real signals of relief — a GOP frontrunner is running on killing the 24% wholesale tax, courts are backing retailers on surveillance fights, and new storefronts keep opening in Detroit and Ann Arbor. Nationally, Eli Lilly just bought into psychedelics, the FDA held a landmark hearing on psilocybin and MDMA-style therapies, and MSO consolidation keeps accelerating even as full federal rescheduling grinds on.

local.text: John James pledges to gut the 24% pot tax — Michigan's GOP governor nominee is promising to "repeal or sharply reduce" the wholesale tax, and cannabis operators are backing him with campaign cash.
High Profile Cannabis opens first Detroit store — Ann Arbor-based C3 Industries backed a Black woman-owned, social-equity dispensary on the city's eastside, its debut Detroit location.
JARS Cannabis scores a win against surveillance overreach — the chain got a Flock license-plate reader removed from outside its Madison Heights store after staff pushed back.
U.P. operator Rize finds a workaround for the tax squeeze — the three-store chain is sustaining growth by splitting the wholesale tax burden with suppliers instead of absorbing it alone.

Tax revenue misses target, but relief could be close — the 24% levy brought in just $37 million in Q2 against a $105 million-per-quarter projection, while bipartisan lawmakers back repeal and the industry's lawsuit heads to trial this month.

national.text: Eli Lilly closes its big bet on psychedelics — the pharma giant's AtaiBeckley acquisition, approved by shareholders Sept. 8, brings drug candidates BPL-003, VLS-01 and EMP-01 into its pipeline.
FDA hearing pushes psilocybin and MDMA-style drugs toward the clinic — regulators gathered expert input this week on therapeutic use of psychedelics, calling the field "much closer to home."
Federal court backs medical marijuana's Schedule III status — the D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge to April's reclassification, leaving the rescheduling order in effect.
Vireo Growth to swallow Planet 13 in latest MSO buying spree — the all-stock deal would give Vireo roughly 265 stores across 15 states, making it one of the largest U.S. cannabis retailers.

Full recreational rescheduling still stuck, but the machinery keeps turning — months after the April order, DEA is now sending detailed compliance questionnaires to state-licensed operators seeking federal protections.
